1.explanation: Wrapping elements into a pool uses the generic replaceElement function (in BpmnReplace.js) to create the new Participant and its processRef. That operation internally triggers a change of the canvas root (via the UpdateCanvasRootHandler.execute method), firing a root.set event. DrilldownCentering listens to root.set and then scrolls/zooms the canvas back to a previously stored viewbox, causing the sudden pan. These three pieces—the replaceElement pool logic, the UpdateCanvasRootHandler root switch, and the DrilldownCentering root.set handler—are the key elements driving the unwanted viewport jump.
1.bug_scenario: When the user takes an existing flat process and “wraps” it into a new BPMN pool (Participant) via the replace-based wrap‐in‐pool operation, the canvas unexpectedly pans/zooms so that the diagram jumps out of the current viewport instead of staying fixed.

2.explanation: Wrapping a process in a pool triggers a new root element (the pool) via UpdateCanvasRootHandler.execute, firing a 'root.set' event. The DrilldownCentering module listens to 'root.set' and restores a stored or default viewbox, resetting pan/zoom. Since no prior viewbox was stored for the new pool root, DrilldownCentering scrolls back to 0,0 and zoom 1, causing the jump. These two classes/functions together are responsible for changing the canvas root and then centering the view erroneously on wrap.
2.bug_scenario: When wrapping an existing process in a BPMN pool (Participant), the canvas viewport suddenly jumps—pan and zoom reset—so the diagram moves out of view instead of staying in its current scroll/zoom position.
